paragraphs: The XJR has been part of the XJ range since 1994, and across its four generations has used three different supercharged engines — from the AJ16 inline-six through to the AJ133S V8. The full breakdown by engine code is below.
about.boldParagraph: The XJR is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 4.0-litre supercharged inline-six fitted to the XJR from 1994 to 1997 (X300 generation). This was the last of the classic Jaguar six-cylinder engines before the switch to V8s. No specific known issue pattern is independently confirmed for this application, but we rebuild it to the same standard as our other XJR engines.

A 4.0-litre (X308, 1997–2003) or 4.2-litre (X350, 2002–2009) supercharged V8. This family powered the XJR through two generations and is generally robust, though we always inspect timing chain components and gaskets during a rebuild.

The 5.0-litre supercharged V8 fitted to the XJR from 2009 to 2019. Known for the timing chain tensioner and guide design flaw, plus water pump bearing/seal failure (see the callout above). We replace the timing chain, tensioners, guides and water pump as standard on every AJ133S rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the XJR spans three distinct supercharged engines across four generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an earlier engine's parts will work on a later car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (AJ16, AJ-V8 or AJ133S) via registration or VIN
Your generation (X300, X308, X350 or X351)
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic XJR quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
